title: gentle in-place compactor and evictor coordinator to reduce KV fragmentation and spillover
author: Marisol Gomez
release_notes: Introduces a background gentle in-place compactor and an evictor-coordinator that reduces KV cache fragmentation and upstream spillover. Expect 12-28% lower spill bandwidth under mixed workloads and smoother P99 latency under high churn.
description: Context: Customers observed elevated spillover and variable token-serving latency under high tenant churn and many small allocations. Existing slab reclaim and synchronous compaction caused latency spikes or required aggressive eviction thresholds. This PR implements a low-priority, rate-limited in-place compactor that cooperates with the evictor to reclaim fragmented slots incrementally and avoid sudden bulk spill events. Summary of changes: 1) new background compactor component (server/kv/compactor.rs) that walks recent free/fragmented ranges using a reservation token to avoid interfering with hot allocations; 2) evictor-coordinator (server/kv/evictor/coordinator.rs) that brokers between eviction decisions and the compactor, preferring gentle reclamation before heavy spill; 3) a soft-reservation metadata field on slabs and segments to enable opportunistic adjacent-slot merging; 4) admission-controller heuristics to postpone large spill flushes when the compactor has sufficient lead time; 5) telemetry hooks and new metrics (kv.compactor.* kv.eviction.coordinator.*) with per-tenant counters for fragmentation score, compaction throughput and deferred-spill windows. Motivation and design rationale: Aggressive immediate compaction or synchronous defrag is costly on latency-critical request paths. By moving compaction to a low-priority worker that only reclaims fragmented regions when safe and by coordinating with the evictor to sequence reclamation and spill actions, we can reduce the amount of data forced to disk/network during peak churn while keeping tail latency bounded. The compactor operates in three modes: background-scan (continuous, low rate), opportunistic-coalesce (inline when allocation touches adjacent free ranges), and emergency-pass (single-threaded fast compaction used only when memory pressure crosses a high watermark). The evictor-coordinator maintains a small window of pending evictions and consults the compactor to see whether reclamation can satisfy the request without spill. Implementation notes: The compactor uses a lightweight two-phase marker to avoid races with concurrent allocators: mark candidate range, attempt in-place pointer remap under a short CAS window, and then publish reclaimed metadata. We added a fast path for ranges that are slab-aligned to reduce pointer complexity. Compaction is bounded by time slices to ensure we never starve foreground request handling. The coordinator exposes a tunable hysteresis (config: kv.eviction.coordinator.hysteresis_ms) and a budget per-tenant (kv.compactor.budget_tokens) so operators can trade compaction CPU vs spill bandwidth. Testing and results: Microbench harnesses added under tools/bench/kv_compaction_bench simulate mixed small-update heavy workloads and tenant-multiplexing. Results: 1) Mixed churn read/write workload reduced network spill bytes by 12-28% (median 19%) depending on update size distribution; 2) P99 token latency improved by up to 18% under heavy churn scenarios where prior behavior produced multi-second spill waves; 3) CPU cost of compaction averaged 2-4% of serving CPU on the test machines with controllable knobs. Rollout plan: Start with default conservative knobs in hosted and dedicated canaries for 2 weeks (config flag kv.compactor.enabled=false by default in older clusters). After stable results, flip on for mainline and include a 2-week monitoring window tracked by the SLO dashboard. Backports: backport candidate for 2025-02 patch release to reduce recurring spill incidents on existing customers. Documentation: added a design doc and operator notes in docs/kv/compaction.md and updated console metrics mapping. Risk and mitigation: main risk is subtle allocator races causing allocation latency regressions; mitigations include extensive unit tests, stress tests in the perf-canary suite, and a safe-kill switch kv.compactor.safemode that disables in-place remaps and falls back to existing eviction path. Related work: references ENG-4117 (spill stabilization) and PRs that improved pager heuristics.

review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Overall design looks sound. Concern: how do we guarantee that in-place remaps won't introduce ABA-style issues with concurrent reads? Please add an assertion and a stress test that targets the CAS window.

Marisol Gomez: Added assertion and a targeted stress test (tools/stress/kv_remap_stress.rs). The remap is guarded by a short CAS and we now publish a generation counter to help clients validate cached pointers.
Liang Zhao: Can we expose a per-tenant budget metric so SRE can quickly see noisy tenants? Also please make hysteresis_ms configurable via environment for private installs.
Marisol Gomez: Added kv.compactor.budget_tokens per-tenant metric and exposed hysteresis_ms in server/config/defaults.yaml. Private installer doc updated.
Priya Nair: Did you measure downstream IO locality changes when compactor moves data? We should ensure compaction doesn't worsen snapshotting behavior.

Marisol Gomez: Measured snapshot IO in bench runs; compaction reduces total spill bytes so snapshot churn decreased in our tests. Added note in docs/kv/compaction.md and a dashboard tile to monitor snapshot IO.
Ethan Brooks: CI reported a flake on Windows builders, looks unrelated to compaction but please add a guard in the bench harness.
Marisol Gomez: Added a Windows skip guard for the bench harness. Reran CI and all checks passed.
